svg.title: Juniper $9$ cipher - how it works
svg.desc: Visual explanation of the Juniper $9$ reversible password obfuscation cipher: alphabet families, weight table, gap function, encryption flow, a worked example, and the anatomy of a full $9$ value.
svg.text: position-based substitution cipher · obfuscation, not real encryption
↻ repeat for each plaintext byte · random filler makes output non-deterministic, yet fully reversible
⚠ no secret key · alphabet and weights are public · anyone with this library can decrypt
ENCODING[0 % 7] = ENCODING[0] = [1, 4, 32] → 3 ciphertext chars encode this byte
③ Advance through ALPHA (random start char = Q, index 0)
⑤ Anatomy of the full $9$ value
filler chars are random and skipped on decrypt · payload grows by 2-4 chars per plaintext byte (weight table)
ℹ different random start each call → encrypt('h') yields a new ciphertext every time · all decrypt identically
